narrative: Fire dominated today's feeds: a synthesis dataset for Australia's 2019–2020 megafires, a global analysis arguing that human and bioclimatic drivers are compounding the fire crisis, and work showing post-fire erosion exporting distinct organic carbon pools from forest landscapes. Climate studies show animals buffering change through behaviour and life history, from Alpine ibex using shaded, rugged microhabitats to hazel dormouse torpor projected to 2080, while mountain mammals and birds are modelled as shifting under combined climate and land-use change. On movement and landscape structure, continent-wide tracking of 200 wildcats highlights forest–grassland mosaics (over half of suitable habitat lies outside protected areas), and newly planted woodlands raised movement of mice, invertebrates, plants and fungi relative to farmland. Population work on eastern grey kangaroos shows that drivers of individual reproductive success often fail to scale up to population recruitment. In invasion and community ecology, plant diversity and belowground microbes jointly decide whether communities resist invasion, while invasive ants and nonnative fishes illustrate lasting disruption. Methods papers continue to push AI and acoustics, including Bacpipe, FloraScanner and an AI-assisted metaweb built from eDNA.
